MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron fires at clause-juncture tokens in informal second-person/instructional prose — the token that opens a new clause or list item right after a completed phrase (sentence-initial "I", a colon introducing a list, the ")" of a numbered step, the comma before a date, or the verb/qualifier starting a new predicate) — while being suppressed on mid-clause copulas/prepositions ("are", "is", "of") and sentence-final periods.

L12·N9412unmasked layer
Weak, low-magnitude neuron with no clean semantic category: it fires on ordinary mid-sentence predicate/complement words that fill a slot in a slightly unexpected way ("a sound **idea**", "a **challenging** opportunity", "what can you **do**", "not **relevant** to me", "was **inspired** by", "The idea **is**"), and is strongly suppressed at the completion of highly formulaic collocations ("it is **simple** to", "**good** news", "in the **case**", "two **weeks** ago) — i.e. it looks like a surprisal/collocation-mismatch signal rather than a topical detector.

Fires on the pivot word of a contrastive/exception clause — the token where a statement contradicts or carves an exception out of the preceding general claim (e.g. "always" after "but we", the negation in "does not affect you"/"don't like", the comma after a contrasting "In Nevada"); it is context-driven, since the same tokens (commas, etc.) get suppressed in non-contrastive contexts.
